## TL;DR

Review round 1 found the same defect class in text that never wraps. Server URLs, discovery messages, form warnings, and failure reasons sat in boxes with no `overflow-wrap`, so one unbroken token overflowed at 375px and was clipped silently. I added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to those four selectors, extended the regression test to pin them, and corrected two false claims in the QA doc. Measurements at 375px now show `scrollWidth` equal to `clientWidth` for every case, and they overflowed without the fix. Device QA (#1162) and iOS are still unverified and need a human.

## Work and rationale

The reviewer's three bullets were one class: text containers that cannot wrap. I searched for every server-supplied text container in the hub, not only the three named. The Edit sheet's `.hint` shows the saved URL. `.warn` shows form errors. `.discovery-message` shows the tailnet message. `.reachability` shows the failure reason in the failure group. The rest of the hub's text is either fixed UI copy or already truncates with an ellipsis, which is deliberate in the picker's `.server-name` and `.server-host`. Those four got `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, with a comment saying why.

To verify, I added a switch to the Playwright script that strips the declarations from the served stylesheet, so the same page can run with and without the fix. Without the fix: the sheet URL measured 558px of content in a 343px box, the failure reason 720px in 317px, and the message 854px in 373px. With the fix every case has `scrollWidth` equal to `clientWidth`. I also took a screenshot of the sheet with a 119-character path URL. It wraps across three lines and stays inside the panel.

I checked the reviewer's other point about the 85-character URL. In the Edit sheet it now fits exactly (343px in 343px). In the picker the host is intentionally single-line with an ellipsis, so its `scrollWidth` is larger than its box. That is truncation by design, not the wrapping defect, so I didn't change it.

The reviewer also said the QA doc made two false claims. The sheet row said "URL wraps inside the sheet" when only the short fixture URLs had been checked. The defect section said the name's start was cut off, but only the row's right end was. I corrected both, and I made the 85-character row state what was measured.

The regression test in `src/ui-app/tests/mobile-hub-picker-layout.test.ts` gained a table-driven case for `.hint`, `.warn`, `.discovery-message`, and `.reachability`. Each asserts `overflow-wrap: anywhere`.

The reviewer also said the QA doc can't be reproduced as written, because the error states depend on interaction. I added numbered steps for the four hand-run flows to the doc's re-run section, including how to inject a long token.

## Approaches tried

I first considered auditing only the three selectors named in review. That would have left the class half-fixed, so I grepped for every `v-if` or interpolated text container in the hub and checked each one's box. Most are fixed copy, so the list stayed at four.

For the test I kept the CSS-declaration approach from round 1. jsdom can't measure wrapping, and asserting the declaration is the only check the suite can run. The browser measurements are the evidence that the declaration does what it should.

## Challenges and blockers

RepoOS had already finalized and committed the round-1 report and emptied the drafts folder, so the round-1 draft is no longer in the worktree. I wrote this round-2 draft fresh.

My own dev server setup caused an earlier problem, already described in the round-1 report. This round I used `localhost` throughout and confirmed the served CSS contained my changes before measuring. I also stopped only the Vite process whose working directory was this worktree.

Vitest run directly still fails on `.vue` imports, as before. The repo wrapper passes all 21 mobile and hub files. I ran the wrapper again after this round's changes.

## Key learnings

A defect class is easier to find by listing the containers than by reading the reported instances. Searching for interpolated text inside fixed-width boxes found the same issue in places the review did not name.

Measure the pre-fix state with the fix stripped in the same harness. Comparing against a number from a different run would not show that the declarations are what change the result.

`docWidth` at 375px does not reveal silent clipping, because `body` has `overflow: hidden`. Check each element's `scrollWidth` against its `clientWidth` instead.

Two items remain for a human. Real-device QA on Android (#1162) is not replaced by this run. There is also no `?fixture=error` route, so the error states still depend on the hand-run steps in the QA doc.
